note.after_visit_summary: Your mood has been stable, and your bipolar II disorder is well controlled on lamotrigine 200 mg daily. You sleep about seven hours regularly and have no significant highs or lows. You are taking a multivitamin each morning. Your gynecologist plans to start you on birth control pills next month, which can lower lamotrigine levels in your blood. To ensure your medication remains effective, we will check your lamotrigine level this week before you start the pill, and again two to three weeks after you begin it. Based on the results, we may need to increase your lamotrigine dose. Consider discussing progestin-only pills or an IUD with your gynecologist, as these are less likely to affect lamotrigine. Continue your multivitamin. If you develop a rash with fever or mouth sores, stop lamotrigine and seek emergency care. If you miss five or more doses in a row, do not restart at 200 mg—call us first. We will check in with you in three months, or sooner if needed. Lab results will be sent to 317 -555 -0172.
